slides.title: Speed or oversight
slides.subtitle: One AppSec platform for Unity
slides.notes: Open on the tension the whole deal turns on: Andie needs tooling engineers never feel, Chris and the new CISO need oversight they can defend. GitHub Advanced Security offers the first without the second. Cycode offers neither. The deck argues Unity can have both.

slides.headline: The recommendation

items.t: Consolidate on Endor Labs: SCA, AI SAST, secrets

items.t: One platform replaces five line items
items.sub: Cycode, planned GitHub buy, Black Duck, Coverity, internal filter

items.sub: The noise that broke Cycode adoption

slides.notes: The ask: $950K to $1.05M per year on a 3 year term, versus about $722K for renewing Cycode ($472K) plus adding GitHub Secret Protection ($250K). This deck walks Unity's own five success metrics, scores both options, and prices the gap. If the room reads two slides, it is this one and the scorecard.

slides.headline: Five tools, one problem

items.desc: $472K a year, all engineers. Search too slow to use
Proposed at $250K a year, secrets only
Live on the Engine, 1,000 developers, adoption rated green
Legacy scanners the Engine team still maintains
A re-scoring layer Unity built to survive the noise

slides.notes: Every line except Endor Labs exists because another line does not work. Cycode's search latency and finding floods pushed Unity to build its own CVSS re-scoring layer into Jira. The Engine team still maintains Black Duck for SBOM and Coverity for SAST. The question is not which scanner, it is how many layers of compensation Unity keeps funding.

slides.headline: Three clocks are running

bullets: Tools engineers avoid are failed controls
AI is writing more of the code

slides.notes: For the new CISO this slide is the history lesson: incident, distrust of the incumbent, engineering led rebuild, this decision. The compromise began with a malicious package and ended with roughly 7,500 exfiltrated repos whose embedded secrets the incumbent never flagged. Deciding late means renewing Cycode by default. Incident details are Unity confidential.

slides.headline: Unity already wrote the test

rows.endor_note: In the PR. 92% average false positive reduction.

rows.comp_note: No manifest free C, C++, C#.
GitHub blocks at push, strong there.

slides.notes: These five metrics are Unity's own, from the September 1 review, in Unity's priority order. Split stack means renewing Cycode and adding GitHub Secret Protection. Two honest credits: GitHub push protection is real, and it comes back on metrics 2 and 5. The next six slides walk the metrics one at a time. Net: Endor Labs 5 of 5, the split stack 1.5 of 5.

slides.headline: Engineer experience is the number one metric

stats.label: minutes per Engine scan, PR comments live

slides.takeaway: The number one metric is already proven at Unity
slides.notes: GitHub is honestly good on this metric for the secrets slice; that credit is real and it is handled on metrics 2 and 5. The Engine rollout ran on the philosophy Unity asked for, noisy findings are worse than under reporting: PR comments first, blocking only when in PR triage ships (CR-391). 92% is the platform average false positive reduction; customers report 91 to 99% of findings eliminated as noise.

slides.headline: Security stays in the loop

left.title: Invisible to everyone
bullets: Smooth for engineers, strong at push
No cross tool policy or thresholds
AppSec cannot see how findings are handled

slides.takeaway: Engineers keep the speed, security keeps the map
slides.notes: This is the metric Chris insisted on and the one GitHub Advanced Security structurally cannot meet: no cross tool policy, no risk thresholds, no centralized exception handling. After the incident, we do not know how findings were handled is not an answer a board accepts. Endor Labs keeps engineers in the PR and gives security the policy engine, the exceptions workflow, and the audit trail.

slides.headline: Risk based control, built in

bullets.sub: A call path proves each flaw

slides.notes: Function level reachability separates a CVE exists somewhere from the vulnerable function is actually callable in Unity's code, with the call path as evidence (19,118 CVEs annotated at function level per the September 2 brief; verify that figure before external use). Ask the room what the internal filter costs to maintain and who owns it when its author leaves. That cost never appears on a renewal quote.

slides.headline: One platform, one policy engine, one number

bullets: C, C++, and C# with no manifests
Replaces Cycode SCA and Black Duck

slides.strip: Already required for the Engine: a second stack is duplicate spend
slides.notes: The consolidation logic is asymmetric: Cycode can never cover the Engine because it cannot scan C, C++, or C# without manifest files, but Endor Labs covers everything Cycode does. Package Firewall (blocks malicious packages at install time, the incident's entry vector, works with Artifactory or standalone) and coding agent governance are the growth path on the same platform, deliberately not in this quote.

slides.headline: Which secrets in 20,000 repos are live right now?

stats.label: average financial damage per leaked secret

bullets: Scans full history, every branch and commit
Marks each secret live or dead
One finding per secret, not fifty
Custom rules for Unity token formats

slides.takeaway: Built for 17 acquisitions worth of history
slides.notes: The incident question is not how many pattern matches exist, it is which credentials are live right now. Validation calls the underlying service and marks each finding Valid, Invalid, or Unvalidated, so triage starts with live credentials. Deduplication collapses the same secret in fifty files into one finding. In the incident the incumbent missed the secrets and open source TruffleHog outperformed it, per the September 2 brief. Unity confidential: do not reuse outside this account.

slides.headline: Hard blocking, without going blind

left.title: Guards the push
bullets: Blocks at push, strong at that moment
No check for whether a secret is live

right.title: Guards before, at, and after
bullets: Blocks before the commit exists, agents included

slides.takeaway: The workflow engineers love, the oversight security needs
slides.notes: Give push protection its due: at the push boundary it is excellent, and it is why GitHub is in this conversation. The gap is before and after that boundary: a pre commit hook stops the secret before it enters history anywhere, the same hooks cover AI coding agents, and validation plus full history scanning answer the incident question. Before presenting: SE validation needed (Matthew or Shruti) on hook rollout mechanics at Unity scale, MDM or endorctl distribution, GitHub Enterprise behind VPN, and agent hooks.

items.label: better findings than Black Duck, per Unity
dependency resolution on the Engine test repo
reachability analysis on the same repo

slides.takeaway: C# support was promised for April and shipped in April
slides.notes: Endor Labs is the only vendor scanning C, C++, and C# without manifest files, which is why it is on the Engine at all. Scan times went from 10 hours to 2 hours to under 30 minutes; PR scans have been live since June; adoption is rated green. The evaluation numbers are Unity's own from October 2025: get champion sign off before showing them to new stakeholders.

slides.headline: Teams at Unity's scale see it hold
slides.notes: All public case studies. Zebra Technologies also cut remediation effort by over 60%. Five9 supports more than 250 developers per security engineer. Egnyte reallocated roughly 40% of AppSec resources. Keep each framing exactly as published; swap in different customers only from the approved social proof set.

slides.eyebrow: WHAT THE PREMIUM BUYS: CODE PRO
slides.label: more true positives than GitHub CodeQL, head to head
slides.source: Endor Labs AI SAST vs CodeQL testing, 2026: 3.6x true positives, 2.8x CWE coverage, 2.7x file coverage
slides.notes: Code Pro is 2,000 of the 3,000 seats, so this is most of what Unity is buying. CodeQL is a strong, respected engine and Endor Labs partners with GitHub; the data is simply the data: 3.6x more true positives, 2.8x more CWE coverage, 2.7x more file coverage. Against Cycode: their SAST is the acquired Bearer engine, strongest in Java, about 10 languages, closed rules. Endor Labs AI SAST covers 41 languages with auditable, configurable rules.

slides.headline: SAST that reasons about code

items.label: findings no other tool caught, runner up 18
more than the strongest traditional tool

slides.takeaway: Catches broken access control and business logic flaws
slides.notes: Hand verified ground truth across 8 real projects in Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, C#, and Go. Roughly 3x the frontier models (2.6x Claude Opus 4.7, 3.5x Codex GPT 5.5) and more than 2x Semgrep OSS. It found a zero day (CVE-2026-55407) in a Rust library, a source to sink flaw with no pattern to grep for. Why now for Unity: Copilot and Cursor are already in use and AI written code is multiplying change volume; rule based SAST cannot reason about access control or business logic. Replaces Coverity on the Engine as well.

slides.headline: The gap is smaller than it looks
slides.notes: Finance framing: this is not a bigger security budget, it is the same problem bought once instead of five times. The hidden tax never shows on a quote: engineering hours on the homegrown filter, Black Duck and Coverity upkeep, triage at Cycode noise levels, and an incident class already realized once ($1.2M average damage per leaked secret). The range is the September 1 figure on a 3 year term; confirm current numbers with the account team before presenting.

slides.label: per developer per month between the two paths
slides.source: Gap of $228K to $328K a year across 3,000 covered seats, from figures shared September 1
slides.notes: The gap between about $722K and the $950K to $1.05M range is $228K to $328K a year. Across 3,000 covered engineers that is $6 to $9 per developer per month. Judge that against the five metric scorecard and a $1.2M average cost per leaked secret. Recompute from the final quote before presenting.

slides.headline: De-risked by design

phases.title: Cycode off
bullets: Code Pro rolls out in waves

slides.notes: The hardest codebase is already deployed and adopted, so this is an expansion of a working system, not a migration gamble. Waves are gated on developer trust exactly like the Engine rollout. The H1 2027 checkpoints reuse the scorecard: false positive rate, PR dwell time, secrets blocked pre commit, findings under central policy, tools retired. Confirm sequencing and the wave plan with Thomas (CSE) before presenting.

slides.text: Five metrics. One option meets all five.
steps: Approve the 2027 consolidation before the December renewal
slides.notes: End on the scorecard, then the ask: $950K to $1.05M a year, 3 year term, 2,000 Code Pro plus 1,000 SCA seats. The 3 year term is the pricing basis; the 2025 two year exception is the procurement precedent, and security prefers multi year.

slides.headline: Alternatives considered

bullets: Endor Labs on Engine, GitHub elsewhere

slides.strip: Only scenario three meets all five metrics
slides.notes: Mirrors the September 2 executive brief Chris has already seen. Scenario one solves the Engine but keeps two vendors and split visibility. Scenario two consolidates scanning but leaves secrets governance outside AppSec, failing metric two. Scenario three is the recommendation this deck prices.
